messages:
Maya (sales): quick thread — Acme POC asking for enterprise commit sizing. they want a 12-week pilot, target steady-state 120 qps peak, avg 40 qps, avg response ~450 tokens, 99p latency <200ms. they asked if reserved GPUs are required or if autoscale+burst works. also price questions from procurement.

Raj (acct): adding context: they want a committed monthly spend number for SOW. procurement also asked about overage rates and what counts toward commit.

Sam (eng-platform): can we get the workload shape? is 120 qps sustained or spiky bursts? that matters for reserved vs autoscale.

Maya (sales): mostly spiky — expected bursts during business hours: 15–20s spikes reaching 120 qps for ~10–20 minutes, baseline ~10–20 qps. they also run a nightly batch of embeddings that hits longer sequences.

Jia (eng-ml): for 450-token responses, per-token cost and KV cache behavior matter. if many requests share prefixes we can leverage prefix caching to cut compute. do we know the prompt variability?

Maya (sales): prompts are fairly templated, ~30% identical prefixes across requests. batch of 50k/day for embeddings overnight (avg 512 tokens).

Oliver (solutions): high-level recommendation: reserved pool + autoscale buffer for spikes. suggested starting point: reserved 4x A10G (or equivalent) for baseline, autoscale max to 12 for bursts. With continuous batching and prefix cache that should meet 99p <200ms for 450 tokens.

Sam (eng-platform): rough config we used for similar customers: 
```
reserved_pool: 4 x a10g
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 12
autoscale_policy: burst_concurrency=120; cool_down=120s; scale_step=2
quantization_profile: int8 (if model supports)
cache: prefix_kv_cache=true; ttl=3600s
```
This assumes we use model variant quantized to INT8; if they want FP16 latency improves but cost up.

Priya (security): security note: private deployment required for their compliance. KMS for keys and audit logs enabled. that doesn't change sizing but will affect network egress patterns and possible cold-starts if on-prem.

Raj (acct): procurement pricing Qs: how do we translate "reserved 4 GPUs" into commit? do we do monthly GPU-hour commit or a flat monthly seat/throughput commit? they prefer flat monthly commit tied to throughput.

Oliver (solutions): we can map to a throughput commitment: e.g., commit X RPS-hours or commit baseline reserved GPU hours. common pattern: commit to N vGPU-hours/month and discounted overage. Example: 4 GPUs reserved * 24h * 30d = 2880 GPU-hours/month baseline. we can translate that into a baseline tokens-per-month estimate and offer a discount bucket.

Maya (sales): procurement pushed back on raw GPU-hours — they want a simpler SLA: baseline throughput of 30 qps sustained with burst capacity to 120 qps and price for overage. can we express pricing that way?

Sam (eng-platform): yes — we can expose a throughput SLO mapping to autoscale config and reserve pool. internally we convert throughput to compute using empirical token/sec profiles. for quoting, we can offer: guaranteed baseline 30 qps (price A), burst pool to 120 qps best-effort (price B), and overage at price C per token.

Jia (eng-ml): for embedding nightly batch, recommend separate job queue to run on off-peak times and use preemptible capacity or a separate dedicated small pool (2 GPUs) to avoid impacting interactive latency.

Raj (acct): action item for pricing: can sales ops produce three pricing tiers: baseline-only, baseline+burst, and baseline+burst+priority-sla? procurement wants numbers this week.

Maya (sales): noted. also security questionnaire flagged data residency and key management — Priya, can you confirm private deployment options and whether HSM/KMS are supported?

Priya (security): confirmed: Private deployment supports KMS (customer-managed) and HSM integrations; we can provide SOC2 artifact snippets. we'll attach a short note for procurement.

Sam (eng-platform): POC plan: 1) spin up dedicated 4-GPU reserved pool in us-east, enable prefix cache, deploy quantized model variant. 2) run synthetic load with the exact prompt mix they provided (Maya to get sample) and measure 99p latency and token/sec. 3) run overnight embedding job on separate pool. 4) capture cost/lateness dashboard from Redwood Console and iterate.

Maya (sales): timeline request from Acme: 2-week POC start next Tue. is that feasible?

Sam (eng-platform): feasible if we have sample prompts + API credentials for testing. estimate spin-up ~48h for reserved pool + config.

Oliver (solutions): I'll draft the exact load script and autoscale knobs. plan to test three configs: (A) reserved-only (4 GPUs, no autoscale), (B) reserved+autoscale (min2 max12), (C) autoscale-only (no reserve, aggressive burst). we'll collect latency, cost, and cold-starts.

Raj (acct): procurement Q: if we do a 3-month commit, can we include a clause that lets them convert reserved GPU-hours into credits if they increase usage? logical to offer flexibility.

Maya (sales): we'll push that as a conversion credit — legal can draft.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: create-reserved-pool a10g x4 for acme-poc — started

Sam (eng-platform): getting this started now. Maya pls upload sample prompt set and expected traffic curve to the thread.

Maya (sales): uploaded prompt set to drive.link/acme-prompts and traffic curve sheet.

Jia (eng-ml): quick note on model choice: if they want highest fidelity we should use fp16 variant for the POC to prove quality, then test int8 for cost tradeoffs.

Priya (security): I'll prepare the short security addendum and confirm data residency in us-east-1.

Maya (sales): thanks team — next steps: Sam/Oliver run tests, Raj prepare pricing tiers, Priya prepare security notes. will sync end-of-week for results. :thumbsup:
